chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskhan from al-Halabi said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the person in ihram riding in the qubbah (a covered saddle or enclosure). He said, 'I like nothing except that he be ill.' I said, 'And the women?' He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.اَلْقُبَّةُ: A covered saddle or enclosure used for riding
key_terms.اَلْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: Can a person in ihram ride in a covered saddle if they are ill?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that riding in a covered saddle (*qubbah*) is generally disliked unless necessitated by illness, establishing a principle of ease within the restrictions of ihram. The Imam explicitly extends this concession to women, highlighting the gender-neutral application of this specific fiqh ruling in Shia jurisprudence. This hadith underscores the pragmatic approach of the Imams in balancing ritual purity with physical comfort during pilgrimage.
